study_id: Medved et al. - 2018 - Improving prediction of heart transplantation outcome using deep learning techniques

eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The study analyzes adult heart transplant recipients using a deep learning neural network to predict post‑transplant survival, published in 2018 as an observational registry analysis, meeting all inclusion criteria.

identification_methods.Sponsorship source: Health Resources and Services Administration contract 234-2005-370011C; Swedish National Infrastructure for Computing; Swedish Heart-Lung Foundation; Swedish Society of Medicine; Region Skåne Research Funds; Donation Funds of Skane University Hospital; Anna-Lisa and Sven Eric Lundgrens Foundation; Crafoord Foundation; Swedish Research Council; eSSENCE program
identification_methods.Comments: Retrospective analysis of the UNOS registry to compare deep learning (IHTSA) and logistic regression (IMPACT) models for heart transplantation outcome prediction.
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Included adult heart transplant patients >17 years from the UNOS registry between Jan 1997 and Dec 2011.
identification_methods.AI Model Architecture: Artificial Neural Network ensemble (deep learning) for IHTSA; logistic regression for IMPACT.
identification_methods.Comparator: IMPACT model (logistic regression) versus IHTSA model (deep learning).
identification_methods.Input Variables: 56 variables extracted; IHTSA uses 43 (recipient and donor), IMPACT uses 18 recipient variables.
identification_methods.Missing Data Handling: Probability imputation using uniform distribution from non‑missing values.
identification_methods.Validation Method: 5‑fold cross‑validation on derivation cohort (1997–2008) and independent test cohort (2009–2011).
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Performance assessed with AUROC, C‑index, DeLong test; recalibrated IHTSA model; Hosmer–Lemeshow goodness‑of‑fit test applied.

population.Inclusion criteria: Adult heart transplant patients >17 years from January 1997 to December 2011
population.Population Notes: Cohort divided into derivation (1997–2008, n=22,263) and test (2009–2011, n=5,597) cohorts
population.Pre-transplant Support: Ventricular assist device in 25% of recipients

interventions_outcomes.Specific Algorithm Name: International Heart Transplantation Survival Algorithm (IHTSA) – deep learning; Index for Mortality Prediction After Cardiac Transplantation (IMPACT) – logistic regression
interventions_outcomes.Intervention Input Data Modality: UNOS registry tabular clinical variables (recipient and donor data)
interventions_outcomes.Number of Predictors: IHTSA uses 43 variables; IMPACT uses 18 variables
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: IHTSA employs an ensemble of artificial neural networks (deep learning) and was recalibrated on UNOS data; IMPACT is a logistic‑regression based risk index using only recipient variables
interventions_outcomes.Reported outcomes in study: One‑year mortality (primary), long‑term survival (C‑index) as secondary
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: Primary endpoint: one‑year mortality; secondary endpoint: all‑cause cumulative mortality over study period
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: Comparison of AUROC and C‑index between IHTSA and IMPACT on the test cohort
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Reported as: Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome group: Heart transplant recipients in the test cohort (2009‑2011)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: Area under ROC for predicting one‑year mortality on a completely held‑out test cohort
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: IHTSA showed superior discrimination to IMPACT with an error reduction of ~11.7% in AUROC
